newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end up on warrant-linked bank buys.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end up on warrant-linked bank buys.

text.p: The Athens bourse closed 0.99 percent higher, driven up by a late buying spree on bank shares linked to a Barings call warrant, brokers said.

"A late buying spree in bank stocks drove up the index substantially," said Yannis Kalogerakis, head of trading at ABN-AMRO Axias Securities. "It must relate to the warrants issued by Barings on a basket of six Greek banking shares."

ING Baring Financial Products (IBFP) will issue 100,000 American style call warrants on a basket of six bank stocks. The issue price is $12.50 per warrant. Sigma Securities is the Greek placement agent.
A Baring source confirmed the late bank purchases related to hedging warrant positions.
"I am awaiting to hear like everybody else the government's policy statements tonight," said Kalogerakis.
Simitis will address parliament on his government's economic, domestic and foreign policy plans on Thursday night.
The Athens general share index closed 0.99 percent, or 9.46 points higher at 963.14 from Wednesday's 953.68 close after opening at 954.19 points.
Turnover was higher at 7.53 billion drachmas on volume of 3.94 million shares boosted by block trades in Titan TTNr.AT, Keranis and Athens Medical.
Gainers led decliners 125 to 80 with 37 issues unchanged on 242 traded. Banks rose 2.20 percent, industrials up 0.37 percent and construction ended higher 0.52 percent. Small-caps rose 1.00 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 547-565 at the close. Shares of OTE telecom OTEr.AT, the underlying, ended up 15 drachmas at 4,070.

The recently launched Merrill Lynch stock index call warrant based on a basket of 23 shares was higher at 201.40-212.00 drachmas. It expires on January 9 1998 with a strike price of 1000. It was in the money at 1057.2.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted lower at 4,851-5,167 drachmas at the close. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
